title: Life cycle assessment and recycling

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Limited raw material
items.clue: One of which the Earth holds a finite amount.

items.label: Recycling
items.clue: Processing a used material so it can be made into something new.

items.label: Life cycle assessment (LCA)
items.clue: Judges the environmental impact of a product from raw materials to disposal.

items.label: Reuse
items.clue: Using a product again without reprocessing its material, like a refilled glass bottle.

questions.stem: A life cycle assessment is carried out on a new electric kettle. Which stages of the kettle's life does the assessment cover?

options.text: Extraction, manufacture, use and disposal, plus transport as a fifth
Manufacturing and packaging only, as that is where pollution comes from
Extracting and processing raw materials, manufacture, use, then disposal
Extraction, manufacture and use, but not disposal if it is recycled

questions.explanation: These are the four stages named in the specification, with transport and distribution counted at each of them.

questions.stem: Which action by an end user reduces the use of limited resources by the greatest amount?

options.text: Recycling each product carefully after using it once
Choosing products whose packaging can be recycled
Recycling as much of the packaging as possible
Buying fewer new products in the first place

questions.explanation: Reduction in use avoids extraction, manufacture, transport and disposal altogether, so it saves the most.

questions.stem: Why does a manufacturer carry out a life cycle assessment on a new product?

options.text: To assess the environmental impact of it across its whole life
To find the profit the product will make once it goes on sale
To measure the pollution given off by the factory that makes it
To produce one objective score that ranks it against rivals

questions.explanation: This is the purpose given in the specification: to assess environmental impact in each of the four stages.

questions.stem: Aluminium drinks cans are collected and recycled instead of being replaced by new aluminium extracted from its ore. Which statement about this is correct?

options.text: Recycling the cans needs no energy at all, unlike extraction
Aluminium ore becomes renewable once the cans are recycled
Less ore has to be mined and far less energy is needed overall
The recycled aluminium is purer than metal made from ore

questions.explanation: Recycling reduces both the use of a limited raw material and the energy needed to obtain the metal.

questions.stem: An LCA is carried out on a poly(ethene) shopping bag. Which of these is counted in the 'extracting and processing raw materials' stage?

options.text: Only the drilling for crude oil, and not the refining that follows it
Growing and harvesting the plants that most plastics are made from
Blowing molten polymer into a thin film to form the bag
Drilling for crude oil and processing it into poly(ethene)

questions.explanation: The stage is 'extracting and processing raw materials', so the drilling and the processing into the polymer both belong to it.

questions.stem: Which statement about the raw materials used to make metals, glass, clay ceramics and most plastics is correct?

options.text: Most plastics are made from plants, so they are a renewable source
They are unlimited, because these products can be recycled
Only metals are limited; glass and clay are unlimited
They all come from limited raw materials found in the Earth

questions.explanation: The specification states that all of these are produced from limited raw materials.

questions.stem: An LCA is carried out on a jar of jam sold in a glass jar. Which of these belongs to the 'manufacturing and packaging' stage?

options.text: Only the work done inside the factory, as transport is its own stage
Moulding the hot glass and boxing the jars for delivery
The cardboard tray is left out, as it is not part of the product
Quarrying the limestone and sand that the glass is made from

questions.explanation: Shaping the product, and making and filling its packaging, are exactly what this stage covers.

questions.stem: A company quarries limestone to make cement. Which of these is the best description of the environmental impact of the quarrying?

options.text: Dust, noise and the loss of habitat around the quarry site
There is no lasting impact, as the site will be landscaped later
The only impact is the fuel burned by the machines there
None, as limestone re-forms quickly and can be quarried again

questions.explanation: Obtaining raw materials from the Earth by quarrying causes exactly these local environmental impacts.

questions.stem: Two washing machines have the same impacts at every stage but one: machine A uses less electricity and less water per wash. Which stage of the LCA does this difference belong to?

options.text: Use and operation during its lifetime, as less energy and water are used
No stage at all, since electricity is used at home and not at a works
Manufacturing and packaging, since the factory sets how efficient it is
Disposal at the end of its useful life, as it will last a long time

questions.explanation: Resources consumed while the machine is in service are counted in the third stage of the LCA.

questions.stem: A glass bottle is returned to the dairy, washed and then filled with milk again. Which term describes what has happened to the bottle, and why?

options.text: Recycling, because the glass has been used for a second time
Reuse, because the bottle is used again as it is
Reduction, because fewer new bottles now need making
Recycling, since the bottle was collected for processing

questions.explanation: The object itself is used again without the material being reprocessed, which is reuse.

questions.stem: In an LCA of tinned food, where is the impact of the lorry journeys that carry the tins to the shops counted?

options.text: In a separate transport stage, added on after the four main stages
In manufacturing and packaging, as the factory arranges delivery
Nowhere, because the lorries belong to a delivery firm
Within each stage, since transport is included at all four stages

questions.explanation: The specification includes transport and distribution at each stage, not as a stage of its own.

questions.stem: Waste glass bottles are crushed and melted, and the glass is then made into new glass jars. Why is this recycling rather than reuse?

options.text: The glass has been reprocessed and made into a different product
It is reuse, because the same glass is being used once more
Recycled glass must always be turned back into bottles
It is reduction, because fewer new jars have to be made

questions.explanation: Crushing and melting reprocesses the material, so the bottles have been recycled, not reused.
